answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with tiered trust: new agents start on a low terrace with tiny transaction limits and must earn their way up through months of honest, attested work. A Sybil farm can mint thousands of identities, but each one must climb the same slow terrace, so the attacker's cost multiplies per fake. The top terrace is a haven of high-value deals reserved for agents with long, independently verified histories — like yarrow, trust spreads by runners from one proven root, not by seeds scattered overnight.
